meta: A man examines a bottle of urine held in his right hand in Antonio Zanchi's painting of about 1650.
about: A man shown half-length looks closely at a bottle of urine that he holds in his right hand. Antonio Zanchi painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1650. Mr. and Mrs. Kessler-Hülsmann of Kapelle op den Bosch gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Louis-François Lejeune's Battle of Aboukir of 1804, showing Napoleon's victory over an Ottoman force in Egypt in 1799.
about: This history painting of 1804 by Louis-François Lejeune shows the Battle of Abukir, fought on 25 July 1799 during the French invasion of Egypt, in which General Napoleon Bonaparte's troops beat an Ottoman force outside Abu Qir on the Mediterranean coast. It was one of three paintings Lejeune showed at the Salon of 1804 at the Louvre, along with his Battle of Lodi.

meta: A young woman in a brocade dress in profile, a Berlin portrait of 1465 now given to Piero del Pollaiuolo.
about: This half-length portrait of 1465, in oil and tempera on a poplar panel, was usually attributed to Antonio del Pollaiuolo, though the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin now gives it to his brother Piero. The museum counts it among its most famous paintings and among the most famous portraits of women of the early Italian Renaissance. The woman is unnamed, shown in a brocade dress with a posture that suggests she sits against a marble embrasure.

meta: The Archangel Michael by Theodore Poulakis, a Cretan painter active in Venice and the Ionian Islands.
about: Theodore Poulakis made this painting of the Archangel Michael. He was active in the Ionian Islands and Venice, studied painting in Venice for over a decade, and sat on the quarantia in Venetian politics. He represented both the Cretan school and the Heptanese school, and is counted a founder of the latter with Elias Moskos. About 130 paintings are attributed to him.

meta: The painter Willem Hendrik Schmidt stands with a brush before a canvas in his self-portrait of about 1840.
about: Willem Hendrik Schmidt, who lived from 1809 to 1849, portrays himself standing with a brush in his hand in front of a canvas, with a maulstick over his left shoulder. The catalog dates it to 1840, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A family waits outside a courtroom for a verdict in Abraham Solomon's Waiting for the Verdict, 1859.
about: A distraught family waits outside a courtroom for the verdict that they hope will clear their loved one. Through the door in the background the red-robed judge can be seen above the somber lawyers in white wigs. Each family member shows a different degree of worry and hope. Abraham Solomon painted Waiting for the Verdict in 1859, and it is in the Getty.

meta: David McClellan, one of Benjamin Trott's portraits painted in 1805 on a yearlong ride through Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Ohio.
about: This portrait and its pair were painted in 1805, after Benjamin Trott set out on horseback for a yearlong journey westward. They are two of the many works he made along the way through Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Ohio, the states that then marked the western edge of the country.

meta: A sculpture of a young boy in Eva Bonnier's studio on Rue Humboldt in Paris, painted in 1886.
about: Eva Bonnier painted this interior of her studio on Rue Humboldt in Montparnasse in 1886, with a sculpture of a young boy. The oil on canvas measures 41 by 32 centimeters. She lived in Paris from 1883 to 1889. Karl Otto Bonnier gave it to the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm in 1910.

meta: A plowed Iowa field in Grant Wood's Fall Plowing of 1931, praising the new steel plowshare.
about: Fall Plowing is an oil painting of 1931 by Grant Wood that shows a plowed field in his home state of Iowa. Wikipedia says it pays tribute to the recently developed walking plow with its steel plowshare, used by farmers across the Midwest then, and stresses the part new technology played in turning prairie into farmland. The area is now on the National Register of Historic Places. The original is in the John Deere collection.

meta: A scholar reclines by a rock watching clouds rise, Ma Lin's painting answering a verse by Wang Wei, about 1256.
about: Poem and painting were once mounted together as one fan and show the teamwork of an imperial patron and a court painter. Emperor Lizong's calligraphy quotes Wang Wei's verse about walking to where the water ends and sitting to watch clouds rise. Ma Lin answers it with this painting of a scholar reclining at the water's edge by a large rock. The view leads across an empty middle ground to a distant mountain, and sparse ink and subtle washes picture the verse.

meta: Noah kneels at a brick altar where a ram burns, a drawing in an oval by Pietro Novelli.
about: Noah kneels at the foot of a brick altar at the right. His sacrifice of a ram lies on the altar among flames, with a cloud of smoke rising. A crowd looks on at the left, and a vase with a handle, perhaps for pouring libations, is in the foreground. The drawing sits inside an oval. Pietro Novelli made it.

meta: Monks read on one bank while a pilgrim rests before a woman with a staff in Antonio Francesco Peruzzini's landscape of about 1690.
about: A river landscape has a woman with a staff and a jug standing on the bank, with a resting pilgrim in the foreground. Across the water two monks sit reading books, and a monastery stands behind. Antonio Francesco Peruzzini painted it as the pendant of another picture in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Elizabeth Thompson's 1875 painting of the 28th Regiment at Quatre Bras, before she became Lady Butler.
about: Elizabeth Thompson painted The 28th Regiment at Quatre Bras in 1875, two years before her marriage made her Lady Butler. She based it on the account of the battle in Captain William Siborne's History of the War in France and Belgium in 1815. The oil on canvas is 97.2 centimeters high and 216.2 wide, and it is in the National Gallery of Victoria in Melbourne.

meta: President James Buchanan in a miniature by John Henry Brown after his own daguerreotype, about 1860.
about: John Henry Brown painted this miniature of the president James Buchanan from a daguerreotype he made himself, and he was well satisfied with the likeness. Buchanan's nephew and ward, James Buchanan Henry, later wrote in a biography that the best likeness of him was a miniature on ivory by Brown of Philadelphia. He remembered Buchanan as over six feet tall, broad-shouldered and portly, with a dignified bearing and strong, well-marked features.

meta: Mary and her mother Anne hold the Christ Child in Joseph Paelinck's Holy Family of about 1820.
about: The Virgin Mary and her mother Anne hold the Christ Child, and Mary's husband Joseph and her father Joachim probably look on. The Getty says the identity of the two older people is debatable, since one reading is that they might be biblical prophets. Joseph Paelinck painted it around 1820.

meta: Juan Sánchez Cotán's Still Life with Game Fowl of about 1600 to 1603, the Art Institute's earliest European still life.
about: Still Life with Game Fowl is the Art Institute's earliest European still-life painting. Still life became an independent genre in the sixteenth century, when artists began to specialize in landscape, portraits and scenes of everyday life. Some, like Juan Sánchez Cotán, grew interested in showing their skill at painting inanimate objects, partly as an expression of the order and variety of the natural world. The museum says his focus changed in 1603.

meta: Louis Buvelot's Summer Afternoon, Templestowe of 1866, an early Australian landscape that inspired Streeton's Golden Summer.
about: Summer Afternoon, Templestowe is an 1866 painting by the Swiss-Australian landscape painter Louis Buvelot. Wikipedia calls it a foundational piece of Australian landscape art and a precursor of Australian Impressionism. It was one of the first purchases of the National Gallery of Victoria in 1869 and is not on display. It was a major inspiration for Arthur Streeton's Golden Summer, Eaglemont of 1889.

meta: A bedchamber corner with an alcove bed and a small commode with a clock, a paneling design by Nicolas Pineau, about 1720.
about: A corner of a bedroom is shown, with half the bed in a niche at the right. The bed has a canopy, and the niche is decorated with a medallion showing a bust. A small corner commode with a clock stands beside it. Nicolas Pineau made the design for paneling around 1720.
